chunks: Muawiya ibn 'Ammar narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who runs between al-Safa and al-Marwah while riding. He said, 'There is no harm, but walking is superior.'

key_terms.السَّعْي: The ritual running/walking between Safa and Marwah
key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa, one of the two hills in Mecca
key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: There is no harm / it is permissible
key_terms.وَالْمَرْوَة: Al-Marwah, the second hill in Mecca

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to ride between Safa and Marwah during Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: In this narration from Sahih al-Tusi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility of Sa'i rituals, affirming that while riding between Safa and Marwah is legally valid (ja'iz), walking is considered superior (afdhal) due to the greater physical exertion and humility it entails. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of distinguishing between the validity of an act and the excellence of its performance, accommodating the needs of the pilgrim while encouraging voluntary asceticism.
